newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Taihang Cement aims to list in Australia.
newsitem.headline: China's Taihang Cement aims to list in Australia.

text.p: Hebei Taihang Cement Co Ltd expects to offer 72 million foreign currency shares and list them on the Australian Stock Exchange in July next year, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
If the offer and listing succeed, Taihang will become the first mainland Chinese company to be listed in Australia, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Taihang is among 38 Chinese domestic firms newly selected by the Securities Commission of the State Council as candidates for overseas listings.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the country's top securities watchdog, signed a memorandum of understanding with its counterpart in Australia in July 1996, and the CSRC recommended Taihang to list shares there, he said.
An underwriter has yet to be selected for the offer, and the pricing has not yet been discussed, he said.
If the issue goes through, Taihang would use the proceeds to start the construction of a 250-million-yuan cement project due for completion in 18 months, the official said.
Taihang, based in the city of Handan in northern Hebei province, currently has total share capital of about 200 million shares, he said without giving a breakdown of the share capital.
Taihang expects net profits of 81.43 million yuan for 1996, compared with 70.39 million yuan in 1995 and 57.93 million yuan the previous year, the official said.
He said Taihang produced 160 tonnes of cement in 1996, ranking it third among Chinese cement producers. It produced 146 tonnes in 1995 and 136 tonnes in 1994.
